title.narrative: Social Dialogue in Combination Country Bangladesh

description.narrative: In six countries Mondiaal FNV will support trade unions to play a prominent role in making trade and economic development more inclusive, and more climate friendly. The policy document of the Minister refers to two transitions, regarding sustainability and digitalisation. For such transitions, Mondiaal FNV refers to ILO’s “Just Transition” agenda, where involvement of both employers’ associations and trade unions are essential. Social dialogue can ensure that in all instances where work patterns or sectoral employment are expected to shift significantly, the consequences for the workers are included in the equation. For the combination-country approach Mondiaal FNV will work in international value chains in the sectors of leather (Bangladesh), horticulture (in Ghana, India and Nigeria), and palm oil (in Colombia and Indonesia). Where possible, we link to Dutch actors in these chains, in view of responsible business conduct and future due diligence legislation. Capacity building for social dialogue can greatly contribute to more sustainable chains. The plans for India have a strong focus on the position of women, in the plans for Colombia and Indonesia the position of women is one of the areas that we will emphasise, for Ghana and Nigeria, the sectoral mapping that we envisage will inform us about the potential for a specific focus on women. International networking on RBC and due diligence, and the trade union experiences in this combination- country approach are expected to consolidate our learning.
